objects.definition: typedef struct JSRuntime JSRuntime;
objects.description: Opaque runtime handle for the QuickJS engine instance. Owns global resources like GC, atoms, and memory allocators. Create with JS_NewRuntime/JS_NewRuntime2 and free with JS_FreeRuntime.

objects.definition: typedef struct JSContext JSContext;
objects.description: Opaque execution context associated with a JSRuntime. Holds per-context state such as global objects, intrinsic objects, and execution settings. Create with JS_NewContext/JS_NewContextRaw and free with JS_FreeContext.

objects.definition: typedef struct JSObject JSObject;
objects.description: Opaque engine-internal representation of a JavaScript object. Not directly constructed by API; JSValue with object tag refers to it.

objects.definition: typedef struct JSClass JSClass;
objects.description: Opaque engine-internal class structure. Not exposed for direct manipulation; use JSClassID and JSClassDef to define custom classes.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t JSClassID;
objects.description: Identifier for QuickJS object classes. Obtain new IDs with JS_NewClassID and register classes with JS_NewClass.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t JSAtom;
objects.description: Atom identifier for interned strings/symbol-like keys. Create/dup/free with JS_NewAtom/JS_DupAtom/JS_FreeAtom.

Discriminated value type representing any JavaScript value (number, string, object, etc.). Representation depends on build flags (NaN boxing, union+tag, or debug checked pointer form). Ownership rules: functions taking JSValue consume ownership; taking JSValueConst borrow; returning JSValue transfers; returning JSValueConst does not. Free with JS_FreeValue/JS_FreeValueRT when you own it.

objects.definition: typedef struct JSGCObjectHeader JSGCObjectHeader;
objects.description: Opaque GC object header used internally for marking. Not user-constructible.
Allocator function table for customizing memory allocation for a runtime. Pass to JS_NewRuntime2.
Aggregated memory usage stats filled by JS_ComputeMemoryUsage and printable with JS_DumpMemoryUsage.
Describes a property key in enumeration results, including whether it is enumerable and its atom.
Property descriptor structure used with get_own_property and related class hooks. JSValue fields follow ownership rules of the API that fills them.
Optional hook table for custom class exotic behaviors overriding default property semantics.
Definition of a custom class: name, finalizer/mark hooks, optional call behavior, and optional exotic methods. Register with JS_NewClass for a JSClassID.
Options for JS_Eval2/JS_EvalThis2 such as flags, filename, and starting line number. version must match JS_EVAL_OPTIONS_VERSION.
Duplicate entry note: already documented above.

objects.definition: typedef void JSFreeArrayBufferDataFunc(JSRuntime *rt, void *opaque, void *ptr);
objects.description: Callback to free external memory for ArrayBuffer/TypedArray when the JS engine releases it.

objects.definition: typedef struct JSModuleDef JSModuleDef;

Union of function pointer types used in JSCFunctionListEntry to specify native functions, accessors, and iterators.

objects.definition: typedef int JSModuleInitFunc(JSContext *ctx, JSModuleDef *m);
objects.description: Signature for C module initialization function passed to JS_NewCModule.

objects.definition: typedef void JSRuntimeFinalizer(JSRuntime *rt, void *arg);
objects.description: Finalizer function type invoked at the end of JS_FreeRuntime via JS_AddRuntimeFinalizer.

objects.description: Job function signature for the job queue; enqueue with JS_EnqueueJob.

Callback to normalize module specifiers for the module loader.
Callbacks to load modules (optionally with import attributes). Register with JS_SetModuleLoaderFunc/JS_SetModuleLoaderFunc2.

functions.name: JS_NewRuntime
functions.description: Create a new QuickJS runtime handle. Use as the top-level owner for contexts and engine state.
requirements: Must be freed with JS_FreeRuntime when no longer needed.

functions.name: JS_SetRuntimeInfo
functions.description: Attach an informational ASCII/UTF-8 string to the runtime, primarily for debugging or diagnostics.
requirements: rt must be a valid JSRuntime* created by JS_NewRuntime/JS_NewRuntime2.
info lifetime must exceed that of rt (per comment).

functions.name: JS_SetMemoryLimit
functions.description: Set the memory usage limit for the runtime; use 0 to disable limiting.
requirements: rt must be a valid JSRuntime*.
limit is a byte count; 0 disables the limit.

functions.name: JS_SetDumpFlags
functions.description: Enable/disable internal debug dump categories by bitmask.
requirements: flags is a bitmask composed of JS_DUMP_* constants.

functions.name: JS_GetDumpFlags
functions.description: Retrieve the current debug dump flags bitmask for the runtime.

functions.name: JS_GetGCThreshold
functions.description: Get the current garbage collection threshold in bytes.

functions.name: JS_SetGCThreshold
functions.description: Set the garbage collection threshold in bytes at which automatic GC may trigger.

functions.name: JS_SetMaxStackSize
functions.description: Configure the maximum JS stack size; use 0 to disable the check.
requirements: stack_size is in bytes; 0 disables maximum stack size check.

functions.name: JS_UpdateStackTop
functions.description: Notify the runtime that the host thread has changed so the engine can recompute stack top for overflow checks.
requirements: Call when changing threads that use the runtime.

functions.name: JS_NewRuntime2
functions.description: Create a new runtime using caller-supplied malloc functions and an opaque pointer passed to them.
requirements: mf may be NULL to use defaults (unknown; not specified).
If provided, function pointers in mf must be valid and follow required semantics.

functions.name: JS_FreeRuntime
functions.description: Dispose of a runtime and all resources owned by it. Finalizers run at the very end in LIFO order.
requirements: rt must be a runtime obtained from JS_NewRuntime/JS_NewRuntime2.
Do not use the runtime or objects after calling.
Registered finalizers should not attempt to use the runtime (per note: runtime is no longer usable).

functions.name: JS_GetRuntimeOpaque
functions.description: Retrieve the user-defined opaque pointer associated with the runtime.

functions.name: JS_SetRuntimeOpaque
functions.description: Associate a user-defined opaque pointer with the runtime.

functions.name: JS_AddRuntimeFinalizer
functions.description: Register a finalizer to be called in LIFO order at the end of JS_FreeRuntime for cleanup of associated resources.
requirements: finalizer must be a valid function pointer; it will be called with rt and arg at the very end of JS_FreeRuntime.
Finalizer must not use the runtime (the runtime itself is no longer usable).

functions.name: JS_MarkValue
functions.description: Mark a JS value and traverse reachable objects for the GC using a custom mark function (for embedding integration).
requirements: val may be any JS value.
mark_func must be a valid function for marking GC objects.

functions.name: JS_RunGC
functions.description: Force a garbage collection cycle.

functions.name: JS_IsLiveObject
functions.description: Return whether the given JS object is currently live (not collected) in the runtime.
requirements: obj must be a JS object value or an object-like JSValueConst.

functions.name: JS_NewContext
functions.description: Create a new JS execution context associated with the runtime.
requirements: rt must be a valid JSRuntime*.
Context must be freed with JS_FreeContext.

functions.name: JS_FreeContext
functions.description: Destroy a JS context and release resources owned by it.
requirements: s must be a context created by JS_NewContext/JS_NewContextRaw.
Do not use the context after calling.

functions.name: JS_DupContext
functions.description: Increment the reference count on a context and return it.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext*.
Result must be balanced with JS_FreeContext when no longer needed.

functions.name: JS_GetContextOpaque
functions.description: Retrieve the user-defined opaque pointer associated with the context.

functions.name: JS_SetContextOpaque
functions.description: Associate a user-defined opaque pointer with the context.

functions.name: JS_GetRuntime
functions.description: Get the runtime that owns the given context.

functions.name: JS_SetClassProto
functions.signature: void JS_SetClassProto(JSContext *ctx, JSClassID class_id, JSValue obj);
functions.description: Set the prototype object for a registered custom class ID.
requirements: class_id must be a registered class ID.
Takes ownership of obj (JSValue parameter semantics).

functions.name: JS_GetClassProto
functions.description: Get the prototype object for a custom class ID.
requirements: class_id must be a registered class ID.
Returns a JSValue; caller must free with JS_FreeValue unless it is JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_GetFunctionProto
functions.description: Get the intrinsic Function.prototype object for the context.
requirements: Returns a JSValue; caller must free with JS_FreeValue unless JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_NewContextRaw
functions.description: Create a new minimal context without installing all intrinsic objects; used to selectively add intrinsics.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicBaseObjects
functions.description: Add the base intrinsic objects (Object, Function, etc.) to a raw context to save memory when customizing.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context, typically created by JS_NewContextRaw.
Should be called before executing code.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicDate
functions.description: Install the Date intrinsic into a raw/minimal context.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicEval
functions.description: Install eval-related intrinsics into a raw/minimal context.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicRegExpCompiler
functions.description: Install the RegExp compiler internals into a raw/minimal context.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicRegExp
functions.description: Install the RegExp intrinsic into a raw/minimal context.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicJSON
functions.description: Install the JSON intrinsic into a raw/minimal context.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicProxy
functions.description: Install the Proxy intrinsic into a raw/minimal context.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicMapSet
functions.description: Install the Map and Set intrinsics into a raw/minimal context.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicTypedArrays
functions.description: Install the TypedArray and ArrayBuffer related intrinsics into a raw/minimal context.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicPromise
functions.description: Install the Promise intrinsic into a raw/minimal context.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicBigInt
functions.description: Install the BigInt intrinsic into a raw/minimal context.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicWeakRef
functions.description: Install the WeakRef intrinsic into a raw/minimal context.

functions.name: JS_AddPerformance
functions.description: Install the performance timing API into the context.

functions.name: JS_AddIntrinsicDOMException
functions.description: Install the DOMException intrinsic (error type) into the context.

functions.name: JS_IsEqual
functions.signature: int JS_IsEqual(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst op1, JSValueConst op2);
functions.description: Perform abstract equality comparison (==) between two values. Returns nonzero for true, 0 for false, or <0 on exception.
requirements: On error returns negative; check for JS_EXCEPTION state via JS_HasException if needed.

functions.name: JS_IsStrictEqual
functions.signature: bool JS_IsStrictEqual(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst op1, JSValueConst op2);
functions.description: Perform strict equality comparison (===) between two values.

functions.name: JS_IsSameValue
functions.signature: bool JS_IsSameValue(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst op1, JSValueConst op2);
functions.description: Perform SameValue comparison semantics (like Object.is).

functions.name: JS_IsSameValueZero
functions.signature: bool JS_IsSameValueZero(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst op1, JSValueConst op2);
functions.description: Perform SameValueZero comparison (like Map/Set key equality where +0 and -0 are equal).

functions.name: js_string_codePointRange
functions.signature: JSValue js_string_codePointRange(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_val, int argc, JSValueConst *argv);
functions.description: Internal/testing-only function: compute/return a range of Unicode code points from arguments. Only used for running 262 tests.
requirements: Returns a JSValue; caller must free with JS_FreeValue unless it is JS_EXCEPTION.
Arguments semantics are test-internal; details not documented.

functions.name: js_calloc_rt
functions.description: Allocate zero-initialized memory via runtime allocator.
requirements: count*size behavior like calloc; may return NULL on OOM.

functions.name: js_malloc_rt
functions.description: Allocate memory via runtime allocator.

functions.name: js_free_rt
functions.description: Free memory previously allocated with js_*_rt using the same runtime.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer returned by js_*_rt or NULL.

functions.name: js_realloc_rt
functions.description: Reallocate memory via runtime allocator.
requirements: ptr must be NULL or allocated with the same runtime.
May return NULL; original ptr remains valid on failure (standard realloc semantics are assumed).

functions.name: js_malloc_usable_size_rt
functions.description: Return the usable size of an allocation from the runtime allocator.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer allocated by the runtime allocator.

functions.name: js_mallocz_rt
functions.description: Allocate zero-initialized memory via runtime allocator.

functions.name: js_calloc
functions.description: Allocate zero-initialized memory tied to a context's allocator.

functions.name: js_malloc
functions.description: Allocate memory tied to a context's allocator.

functions.name: js_free
functions.description: Free memory previously allocated with js_* using the same context.
requirements: ptr must be from js_* with same context or NULL.

functions.name: js_realloc
functions.description: Reallocate memory via context allocator.
requirements: ptr must be NULL or allocated with same context.
May return NULL; original ptr remains valid on failure (typical realloc semantics are assumed).

functions.name: js_malloc_usable_size
functions.description: Return the usable size of an allocation from the context allocator.
requirements: ptr must be from context allocator.

functions.name: js_realloc2
functions.description: Reallocate memory via context allocator and optionally report slack/extra usable space.
requirements: ptr must be NULL or allocated with same context.
pslack may be NULL or out param.

functions.name: js_mallocz
functions.description: Allocate zero-initialized memory via context allocator.

functions.name: js_strdup
functions.description: Duplicate a C string using the context allocator.
requirements: str must be a null-terminated C string.

functions.name: js_strndup
functions.description: Duplicate up to n bytes from a string, ensuring NUL termination, via the context allocator.
requirements: s must be at least n bytes readable (or a C string of length >= n).

functions.name: JS_ComputeMemoryUsage
functions.description: Fill a JSMemoryUsage struct with current memory usage statistics for the runtime.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to writable JSMemoryUsage.

functions.name: JS_DumpMemoryUsage
functions.description: Print a human-readable summary of memory usage to a FILE stream.
requirements: fp must be a valid FILE* opened for writing.
s must point to a JSMemoryUsage previously filled (e.g., by JS_ComputeMemoryUsage).
rt must be the runtime the stats correspond to.

functions.name: JS_NewAtomLen
functions.signature: JSAtom JS_NewAtomLen(JSContext *ctx, const char *str, size_t len);
functions.description: Create/intern an atom from a byte string of given length (ASCII or UTF-8).
requirements: str must point to at least len bytes; no NUL terminator required.

functions.name: JS_NewAtom
functions.description: Create/intern an atom from a NUL-terminated byte string (ASCII or UTF-8).
requirements: str must be a NUL-terminated C string.

functions.name: JS_NewAtomUInt32
functions.description: Create/intern an atom representing an unsigned 32-bit integer property key.

functions.name: JS_DupAtom
functions.description: Increment the reference to an atom in the context and return it.
requirements: v must be a valid atom obtained from QuickJS.

functions.name: JS_DupAtomRT
functions.description: Increment the reference to an atom in the runtime and return it (runtime-level).
requirements: v must be a valid atom.

functions.name: JS_FreeAtom
functions.description: Decrement/free an atom reference in the context.
requirements: v must be a valid atom previously acquired.

functions.name: JS_FreeAtomRT
functions.description: Decrement/free an atom reference at runtime level.
requirements: v must be a valid atom previously acquired.

functions.name: JS_AtomToValue
functions.description: Convert an atom to a JS value (string or symbol).
requirements: Returns a JSValue; caller must free with JS_FreeValue unless JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_AtomToString
functions.description: Convert an atom to a JS string value.
requirements: Returns a JSValue; caller must free with JS_FreeValue unless JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_AtomToCStringLen
functions.description: Get a UTF-8 C string for an atom, optionally returning its byte length. Must be freed with JS_FreeCString.
requirements: Returned pointer must be freed with JS_FreeCString(ctx, ptr).

functions.name: JS_ValueToAtom
functions.description: Intern a JS value (string or number) as an atom and return its atom ID.
requirements: val must be convertible to an atom (typically string/symbol or numeric property key).

functions.name: JS_NewClassID
functions.description: Allocate a new class ID and optionally store it at pclass_id.
requirements: pclass_id may be NULL or a writable pointer.

functions.name: JS_GetClassID
functions.description: If v is an object, return its class ID; otherwise return JS_INVALID_CLASS_ID.
requirements: v may be any JS value.

functions.name: JS_NewClass
functions.signature: int JS_NewClass(JSRuntime *rt, JSClassID class_id, const JSClassDef *class_def);
functions.description: Register a new custom class with the runtime using the provided class definition.
requirements: class_id must be allocated (e.g., via JS_NewClassID).
class_def must point to a valid JSClassDef that remains valid for the lifetime of the runtime (info lifetime note applies to similar APIs).

functions.name: JS_IsRegisteredClass
functions.description: Return true if the given class ID is registered with the runtime.

functions.name: JS_GetClassName
functions.description: Return the class name atom for a registered class; returns JS_ATOM_NULL if id is not registered. Must be freed with JS_FreeAtom.
requirements: If a non-null atom is returned, caller must free it with JS_FreeAtomRT/JS_FreeAtom (per comment).

functions.name: JS_NewNumber
functions.description: Creates a new JavaScript Number from a C double. Returns a JSValue representing the number.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, live JSContext.
On success, the returned JSValue must be freed with JS_FreeValue(ctx, value) by the caller.
If an exception occurs (e.g., out-of-memory), a JS_EXCEPTION value may be returned; callers should check with JS_IsException and retrieve details with JS_GetException.

functions.name: JS_NewBigInt64
functions.description: Creates a new JavaScript BigInt from a signed 64-bit integer.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, live JSContext.
Returned JSValue transfers ownership to the caller; free with JS_FreeValue(ctx, value).
On failure, returns JS_EXCEPTION; check with JS_IsException and JS_GetException.

functions.name: JS_NewBigUint64
functions.description: Creates a new JavaScript BigInt from an unsigned 64-bit integer.
requirements: Caller must free the returned JSValue with JS_FreeValue(ctx, value).

functions.name: JS_Throw
functions.description: Throws the given JS error object in the context. Transfers ownership of obj to the engine and sets the pending exception.
requirements: obj is consumed; do not use or free it after calling.
Returns JS_EXCEPTION; typical use is to return its result from C functions that implement JS callables.

functions.name: JS_GetException
functions.description: Retrieves and clears the current pending exception. Returns the exception object or JS_NULL/JS_UNDEFINED if none (implementation-defined).
requirements: Returned JSValue must be freed by the caller with JS_FreeValue(ctx, value).

functions.name: JS_HasException
functions.description: Checks if a pending exception is set on the context.

functions.name: JS_IsError
functions.description: Returns true if the value is an Error object.
requirements: val must be a valid JSValueConst (not consumed).

functions.name: JS_IsUncatchableError
functions.description: Returns true if the error is marked uncatchable.
requirements: val must be a valid JSValueConst.

functions.name: JS_SetUncatchableError
functions.description: Marks an error value as uncatchable in the given context.
requirements: val must be an Error object or suitable value; it is not consumed (do not free here).

functions.name: JS_ClearUncatchableError
functions.description: Clears the uncatchable flag on the given error value.
requirements: val is not consumed; caller retains ownership.

functions.name: JS_ResetUncatchableError
functions.description: Convenience helper that retrieves the pending exception, clears its uncatchable flag, and rethrows it as the current exception.

functions.name: JS_NewError
functions.description: Creates a new generic Error object.
requirements: Caller must free the returned JSValue with JS_FreeValue(ctx, value).

functions.name: JS_NewInternalError
functions.description: Creates a new InternalError with a formatted message.
requirements: fmt must be a valid printf-style format string; additional variadic arguments must match the format.
Returned JSValue must be freed by the caller.

functions.name: JS_NewPlainError
functions.description: Creates a new Error (plain error type) with a formatted message.
requirements: fmt must be a valid printf-style format string with matching arguments.
Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_NewRangeError
functions.description: Creates a new RangeError with a formatted message.
requirements: fmt and arguments must be valid.
Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_NewReferenceError
functions.description: Creates a new ReferenceError with a formatted message.
requirements: fmt and arguments must be valid.
Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_NewSyntaxError
functions.description: Creates a new SyntaxError with a formatted message.
requirements: fmt and arguments must be valid.
Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_NewTypeError
functions.description: Creates a new TypeError with a formatted message.
requirements: fmt and arguments must be valid.
Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_ThrowInternalError
functions.description: Creates and throws an InternalError with a formatted message. Returns JS_EXCEPTION.
requirements: fmt and arguments must be valid.
Return value is typically propagated directly from a C function.

functions.name: JS_ThrowPlainError
functions.description: Creates and throws a generic Error with a formatted message. Returns JS_EXCEPTION.
requirements: fmt and arguments must be valid.

functions.name: JS_ThrowRangeError
functions.description: Creates and throws a RangeError with a formatted message. Returns JS_EXCEPTION.
requirements: fmt and arguments must be valid.

functions.name: JS_ThrowReferenceError
functions.description: Creates and throws a ReferenceError with a formatted message. Returns JS_EXCEPTION.
requirements: fmt and arguments must be valid.

functions.name: JS_ThrowSyntaxError
functions.description: Creates and throws a SyntaxError with a formatted message. Returns JS_EXCEPTION.
requirements: fmt and arguments must be valid.

functions.name: JS_ThrowTypeError
functions.description: Creates and throws a TypeError with a formatted message. Returns JS_EXCEPTION.
requirements: fmt and arguments must be valid.

functions.name: JS_ThrowDOMException
functions.signature: JSValue JS_ThrowDOMException(JSContext *ctx, const char *name, JS_PRINTF_FORMAT const char *fmt, ...);
functions.description: Creates and throws a DOMException with a given name and formatted message. Returns JS_EXCEPTION.
requirements: name must be a valid C string (ASCII/UTF-8).
fmt and arguments must be valid.

functions.name: JS_ThrowOutOfMemory
functions.description: Throws an out-of-memory error. Returns JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_FreeValue
functions.description: Decrements the reference count and frees the JSValue if needed. Use when caller owns the value.
requirements: v must be a valid JSValue owned by the caller (not previously freed or consumed).

functions.name: JS_FreeValueRT
functions.description: Same as JS_FreeValue but takes a JSRuntime instead of JSContext.
requirements: rt must be a valid, live JSRuntime.
v must be a valid JSValue owned by the caller.

functions.name: JS_DupValue
functions.description: Duplicates a value (increments reference count) and returns a new owned JSValue.
requirements: Returned JSValue must be freed by caller.

functions.name: JS_DupValueRT
functions.description: Duplicates a value using a JSRuntime reference.
requirements: Returned JSValue must be freed by caller.

functions.name: JS_ToBool
functions.description: Converts a JS value to boolean per JS semantics. Returns 0 or 1, or -1 on exception (with a pending exception set).
requirements: Caller must handle -1 return indicating JS_EXCEPTION and retrieve the exception if needed.

functions.name: JS_ToNumber
functions.description: Converts a value to a Number object/value per JS semantics. Returns a JSValue number or JS_EXCEPTION on failure.
requirements: On success, free returned JSValue. On failure, handle JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_ToInt32
functions.description: Converts a value to a 32-bit signed integer per JS semantics. Returns 0 on success, -1 on exception.
requirements: pres must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the result.
Caller must check for -1 and retrieve the exception if needed.

functions.name: JS_ToInt64
functions.description: Converts a value to a 64-bit signed integer. Returns 0 on success, -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_ToIndex
functions.description: Converts a value to an index (non-negative integer) per JS ToIndex semantics. Returns 0 on success, -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_ToFloat64
functions.description: Converts a value to a double per JS semantics. Returns 0 on success, -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_ToBigInt64
functions.description: Converts a value to a BigInt and then to a signed 64-bit integer. Returns an exception if the input is a Number. Returns 0 on success, -1 on exception.
requirements: Input must not be a Number; otherwise an exception is thrown.

functions.name: JS_ToBigUint64
functions.description: Converts a value to a BigInt and then to an unsigned 64-bit integer. Returns an exception if the input is a Number. Returns 0 on success, -1 on exception.
requirements: Input must not be a Number; otherwise an exception is thrown.

functions.name: JS_ToInt64Ext
functions.description: Converts a value to a 64-bit integer, allowing BigInt inputs as well. Returns 0 on success, -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_NewStringLen
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewStringLen(JSContext *ctx, const char *str1, size_t len1);
functions.description: Creates a new JS string from a byte buffer with explicit length. Assumes ASCII or UTF-8; does not require a terminating NUL.
requirements: str1 must point to at least len1 bytes; content should be ASCII or UTF-8.
Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_NewStringUTF16
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewStringUTF16(JSContext *ctx, const uint16_t *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Creates a new JS string from a UTF-16 buffer of len code units in native endianness. Does not validate UTF-16; may contain unmatched surrogates.
requirements: buf must point to at least len uint16_t code units; not NUL-terminated.
Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_NewAtomString
functions.description: Creates a new JS string from an atomized C string (interning may be applied).
requirements: str must be a NUL-terminated C string (ASCII/UTF-8).
Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_ToString
functions.description: Converts a value to a String per JS semantics. Returns the string value or JS_EXCEPTION on failure.
requirements: Caller must free returned JSValue. Handle JS_EXCEPTION on failure.

functions.name: JS_ToPropertyKey
functions.description: Converts a value to a property key (string or symbol) per JS ToPropertyKey semantics.
requirements: Caller must free the returned JSValue or handle JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_ToCStringLen2
functions.signature: const char *JS_ToCStringLen2(JSContext *ctx, size_t *plen, JSValueConst val1, bool cesu8);
functions.description: Converts a JS value to a C string buffer. Returns a pointer to an internal heap buffer that must be freed with JS_FreeCString. If plen is provided, it receives the byte length. If cesu8 is true, CESU-8 encoding is used.
requirements: Returned pointer must be freed with JS_FreeCString(ctx, ptr).
The returned string is not necessarily NUL-terminated if plen is used? (Unknown; typical QuickJS returns NUL-terminated.)

functions.name: JS_ToCStringLenUTF16
functions.description: Converts a JS value to a UTF-16 buffer in native endianness. Returns a pointer to an internal buffer that must be freed with JS_FreeCStringUTF16. The string is not NUL-terminated and can contain unmatched surrogates. plen receives the length in uint16_t units.
requirements: Returned pointer must be freed with JS_FreeCStringUTF16(ctx, ptr).

functions.name: JS_FreeCString
functions.description: Frees a C string buffer previously obtained from JS_ToCString* or JS_AtomToCString*.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer previously returned by a corresponding QuickJS API that requires freeing with JS_FreeCString.

functions.name: JS_FreeCStringRT
functions.description: Frees a C string buffer using a JSRuntime reference.
requirements: ptr must come from a compatible allocation returned by QuickJS APIs requiring RT free.

functions.name: JS_FreeCStringUTF16
functions.description: Frees a UTF-16 buffer returned by JS_ToCStringLenUTF16.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer previously returned by JS_ToCStringLenUTF16/JS_ToCStringUTF16.

functions.name: JS_FreeCStringRT_UTF16
functions.description: Frees a UTF-16 buffer using a JSRuntime reference.
requirements: ptr must come from a compatible QuickJS UTF-16 allocation to be freed at runtime scope.

functions.name: JS_NewObjectProtoClass
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewObjectProtoClass(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst proto, JSClassID class_id);
functions.description: Creates a new object with the specified prototype and custom class ID.
requirements: class_id must be a registered class ID if using custom classes.
Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_NewObjectClass
functions.description: Creates a new object instance of a registered custom class.
requirements: class_id must refer to a class previously registered with JS_NewClass.
Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_NewObjectProto
functions.description: Creates a new plain object with the specified prototype.
requirements: Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_NewObject
functions.description: Creates a new plain object with the default Object prototype.
requirements: Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_NewObjectFrom
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewObjectFrom(JSContext *ctx, int count, const JSAtom *props, const JSValue *values);
functions.description: Creates a new object from arrays of property atoms and values. Takes ownership of the provided values.
requirements: props must point to count valid JSAtom entries.
values must point to count JSValue entries; function takes ownership of the JSValue elements (caller must not free them after).
Caller must free the returned object value.

functions.name: JS_NewObjectFromStr
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewObjectFromStr(JSContext *ctx, int count, const char **props, const JSValue *values);
functions.description: Creates a new object from arrays of property names (C strings) and values. Takes ownership of the provided values.
requirements: props must point to count NUL-terminated C strings (ASCII/UTF-8).
values must point to count JSValue entries; values are consumed.
Caller must free the returned object value.

functions.name: JS_ToObject
functions.description: Converts a value to an object per JS ToObject semantics. For objects returns the same object; for primitives wraps as object. Returns JS_EXCEPTION on failure (e.g., null/undefined).
requirements: Caller must free the returned JSValue or handle JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_ToObjectString
functions.description: Converts a value to an object and then to its string representation. Exact behavior not further documented in header.
requirements: Caller must free the returned JSValue or handle JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_IsFunction
functions.description: Returns true if the value is a function object.

functions.name: JS_IsConstructor
functions.description: Returns true if the value is a constructor function (has constructor bit set).

functions.name: JS_SetConstructorBit
functions.signature: bool JS_SetConstructorBit(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst func_obj, bool val);
functions.description: Sets or clears the constructor bit on a function object.
requirements: func_obj must be a function object; it is not consumed.

functions.name: JS_IsRegExp
functions.description: Returns true if the value is a RegExp object.

functions.name: JS_IsMap
functions.description: Returns true if the value is a Map object.

functions.name: JS_IsSet
functions.description: Returns true if the value is a Set object.

functions.name: JS_IsWeakRef
functions.description: Returns true if the value is a WeakRef object.

functions.name: JS_IsWeakSet
functions.description: Returns true if the value is a WeakSet object.

functions.name: JS_IsWeakMap
functions.description: Returns true if the value is a WeakMap object.

functions.name: JS_IsDataView
functions.description: Returns true if the value is a DataView object.

functions.name: JS_NewArray
functions.description: Creates a new Array object.
requirements: Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_NewArrayFrom
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewArrayFrom(JSContext *ctx, int count, const JSValue *values);
functions.description: Creates a new Array and fills it with the provided elements. Takes ownership of the provided values array elements.
requirements: values must point to count JSValue entries; values are consumed by the function.
Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_IsArray
functions.description: Returns true if the value is an Array. Note: does not punch through proxies; see comments in header.

functions.name: JS_IsProxy
functions.description: Returns true if the value is a Proxy object.

functions.name: JS_GetProxyTarget
functions.description: Returns the target object of a Proxy.
requirements: proxy must be a Proxy object; not consumed.
Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_GetProxyHandler
functions.description: Returns the handler object of a Proxy.
requirements: proxy must be a Proxy object; not consumed.
Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_NewProxy
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewProxy(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst target, JSValueConst handler);
functions.description: Creates a new Proxy object from target and handler.
requirements: target and handler are not consumed.
Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_NewDate
functions.description: Creates a new Date object initialized from milliseconds since epoch.
requirements: Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_IsDate
functions.description: Returns true if the value is a Date object.

functions.name: JS_GetProperty
functions.signature: JSValue JS_GetProperty(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, JSAtom prop);
functions.description: Gets a property from an object by atom key.
requirements: this_obj must be an object; not consumed.
prop must be a valid JSAtom.
Caller must free the returned JSValue or handle JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_GetPropertyUint32
functions.signature: JSValue JS_GetPropertyUint32(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, uint32_t idx);
functions.description: Gets a property by uint32 index key.
requirements: Caller must free the returned JSValue or handle JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_GetPropertyInt64
functions.signature: JSValue JS_GetPropertyInt64(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, int64_t idx);
functions.description: Gets a property by int64 index key.
requirements: Caller must free returned value or handle JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_GetPropertyStr
functions.signature: JSValue JS_GetPropertyStr(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, const char *prop);
functions.description: Gets a property by C string name.
requirements: prop must be a NUL-terminated C string (ASCII/UTF-8).
Caller must free returned value or handle JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_SetProperty
functions.signature: int JS_SetProperty(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, JSAtom prop, JSValue val);
functions.description: Sets a property by atom key. Takes ownership of val. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure (depending on flags), or -1 on exception.
requirements: prop must be a valid atom.
val is consumed; do not reuse or free it after call.
Caller must handle return value semantics and exceptions.

functions.name: JS_SetPropertyUint32
functions.signature: int JS_SetPropertyUint32(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, uint32_t idx, JSValue val);
functions.description: Sets a property by uint32 index. Takes ownership of val.

functions.name: JS_SetPropertyInt64
functions.signature: int JS_SetPropertyInt64(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, int64_t idx, JSValue val);
functions.description: Sets a property by int64 index. Takes ownership of val.

functions.name: JS_SetPropertyStr
functions.signature: int JS_SetPropertyStr(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, const char *prop, JSValue val);
functions.description: Sets a property by name string. Takes ownership of val.
requirements: prop must be a NUL-terminated C string.

functions.name: JS_HasProperty
functions.signature: int JS_HasProperty(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, JSAtom prop);
functions.description: Checks whether an object has a property. Returns >0 if present, 0 if not, or -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_IsExtensible
functions.description: Returns whether the object is extensible. Returns 1 for true, 0 for false, or -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_PreventExtensions
functions.description: Prevents new properties from being added to the object. Returns 0 on success, -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_DeleteProperty
functions.signature: int JS_DeleteProperty(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst obj, JSAtom prop, int flags);
functions.description: Deletes a property from an object by atom. Returns <0 on exception or true/false per deletion semantics.
requirements: flags may include JS_PROP_THROW, JS_PROP_THROW_STRICT, etc.

functions.name: JS_SetPrototype
functions.signature: int JS_SetPrototype(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst obj, JSValueConst proto_val);
functions.description: Sets the prototype of an object. Returns 0 on success, -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_GetPrototype
functions.description: Gets the prototype of a value/object. Returns the prototype or JS_EXCEPTION.
requirements: Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_GetLength
functions.description: Retrieves the length property (array-like) as int64. Returns 0 on success, -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_SetLength
functions.signature: int JS_SetLength(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst obj, int64_t len);
functions.description: Sets the length property on array-like objects. Returns 0 on success, -1 on exception.
requirements: len should be >= 0 (implied by JS semantics).

functions.name: JS_SealObject
functions.description: Seals an object (prevents addition/removal of properties; existing props non-configurable). Returns 0 on success, -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_FreezeObject
functions.description: Freezes an object (non-extensible; properties non-configurable and non-writable where applicable). Returns 0 on success, -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_GetOwnPropertyNames
functions.signature: int JS_GetOwnPropertyNames(JSContext *ctx, JSPropertyEnum **ptab, uint32_t *plen, JSValueConst obj, int flags);
functions.description: Enumerates own property keys of obj according to flags. On success, *ptab is set to an array of length *plen; must be freed with JS_FreePropertyEnum.
requirements: ptab must be non-NULL; on success, free with JS_FreePropertyEnum(ctx, *ptab, *plen).
flags control which keys (strings, symbols, private, enumerable) are included.

functions.name: JS_GetOwnProperty
functions.signature: int JS_GetOwnProperty(JSContext *ctx, JSPropertyDescriptor *desc, JSValueConst obj, JSAtom prop);
functions.description: Gets the own property descriptor for a property. Returns 1 if exists (and fills desc if not NULL), 0 if not, or <0 on exception.
requirements: desc may be NULL or a valid pointer to receive descriptor; if non-NULL, caller must later free any JSValues inside per QuickJS API expectations (unknown specifics).

functions.name: JS_FreePropertyEnum
functions.description: Frees an array previously returned by JS_GetOwnPropertyNames.
requirements: tab must be a pointer previously returned by JS_GetOwnPropertyNames.
len must match the array length provided by JS_GetOwnPropertyNames.

functions.name: JS_Call
functions.signature: JSValue JS_Call(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst func_obj, JSValueConst this_obj, int argc, JSValueConst *argv);
functions.description: Calls a JS function with a specified this value and arguments.
requirements: func_obj must be a callable; not consumed.
argv must point to argc JSValueConst entries; not consumed.
Caller must free returned JSValue or handle JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_Invoke
functions.signature: JSValue JS_Invoke(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_val, JSAtom atom, int argc, JSValueConst *argv);
functions.description: Invokes a method on an object by atom name with arguments.
requirements: Caller must free returned JSValue or handle JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_CallConstructor
functions.signature: JSValue JS_CallConstructor(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst func_obj, int argc, JSValueConst *argv);
functions.description: Calls a function as a constructor (new) with arguments.
requirements: func_obj must be a constructor (or have constructor bit); not consumed.
Caller must free returned JSValue or handle JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_CallConstructor2
functions.signature: JSValue JS_CallConstructor2(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst func_obj, JSValueConst new_target, int argc, JSValueConst *argv);
functions.description: Calls a constructor with an explicit new.target and arguments.
requirements: Caller must free returned JSValue or handle JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_DetectModule
functions.description: Naively detects whether source code parses as a module. Returns false if parser support is disabled at build time.
requirements: input must point to input_len bytes of ASCII/UTF-8 JavaScript source.

functions.name: JS_Eval
functions.signature: JSValue JS_Eval(JSContext *ctx, const char *input, size_t input_len, const char *filename, int eval_flags);
functions.description: Compiles and evaluates JavaScript source. input must be zero-terminated at input[input_len]. Returns the evaluation result or JS_EXCEPTION.
requirements: input must have a NUL terminator at input[input_len] (zero-terminated).
filename must be a NUL-terminated C string naming the source.
eval_flags must be a combination of JS_EVAL_TYPE_* and JS_EVAL_FLAG_* constants.
Caller must free returned JSValue or handle JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_Eval2
functions.signature: JSValue JS_Eval2(JSContext *ctx, const char *input, size_t input_len, JSEvalOptions *options);
functions.description: Compiles and evaluates JavaScript using an options structure (versioned). Returns result or JS_EXCEPTION.
requirements: input must be zero-terminated at input[input_len].
options must be either NULL or point to a valid JSEvalOptions with version set to JS_EVAL_OPTIONS_VERSION for ABI-compatible fields.
Caller must free returned JSValue or handle JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_EvalThis
functions.signature: JSValue JS_EvalThis(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, const char *input, size_t input_len, const char *filename, int eval_flags);
functions.description: Like JS_Eval but sets a specific this value during evaluation.
requirements: input must be zero-terminated at input[input_len].
Caller must free returned JSValue or handle JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_EvalThis2
functions.signature: JSValue JS_EvalThis2(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, const char *input, size_t input_len, JSEvalOptions *options);
functions.description: Like JS_Eval2 but with an explicit this value.
requirements: input must be zero-terminated at input[input_len].
Caller must free returned JSValue or handle JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_GetGlobalObject
functions.description: Returns the global object for the context.
requirements: Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_IsInstanceOf
functions.signature: int JS_IsInstanceOf(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst val, JSValueConst obj);
functions.description: Implements the instanceof check. Returns 1 if val instanceof obj, 0 if not, or -1 on exception.

functions.name: JS_DefineProperty
functions.signature: int JS_DefineProperty(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, JSAtom prop, JSValueConst val, JSValueConst getter, JSValueConst setter, int flags);
functions.description: Defines or updates a property with descriptor fields based on flags and provided values/getter/setter. Returns 0/1 per spec or -1 on exception.
requirements: flags should include JS_PROP_HAS_* bits indicating which fields are present; may also include JS_PROP_THROW/STRICT.

functions.name: JS_DefinePropertyValue
functions.signature: int JS_DefinePropertyValue(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, JSAtom prop, JSValue val, int flags);
functions.description: Defines a property with a value. Takes ownership of val. Returns 0/1 or -1 on exception.
requirements: flags may include JS_PROP_HAS_* and JS_PROP_THROW/STRICT.

functions.name: JS_DefinePropertyValueUint32
functions.signature: int JS_DefinePropertyValueUint32(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, uint32_t idx, JSValue val, int flags);
functions.description: Defines a property by index with a value. Takes ownership of val.

functions.name: JS_DefinePropertyValueStr
functions.signature: int JS_DefinePropertyValueStr(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, const char *prop, JSValue val, int flags);
functions.description: Defines a property by name string with a value. Takes ownership of val.
requirements: prop must be a NUL-terminated C string.

functions.name: JS_DefinePropertyGetSet
functions.signature: int JS_DefinePropertyGetSet(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj, JSAtom prop, JSValue getter, JSValue setter, int flags);
functions.description: Defines accessor property with getter and/or setter. Takes ownership of getter and setter values.
requirements: getter and setter are consumed (do not free afterwards).
flags control behavior; may include JS_PROP_HAS_* and JS_PROP_THROW/STRICT.

functions.name: JS_SetOpaque
functions.description: Associates a native pointer with a custom class instance. Only supported for custom classes. Returns 0 on success, <0 otherwise.
requirements: obj must be an object of a custom class that supports opaque data.
opaque may be NULL or any pointer; ownership/lifetime managed by caller.

functions.name: JS_GetOpaque
functions.description: Retrieves the opaque pointer previously associated with obj of the given class ID, or NULL if class ID does not match.
requirements: class_id should match the object's class.

functions.name: JS_GetOpaque2
functions.description: Like JS_GetOpaque but may throw an exception if obj is not of the expected class. Returns the opaque pointer or NULL.
requirements: obj must be an object of the given class; otherwise an exception may be thrown (returns NULL).

functions.name: JS_GetAnyOpaque
functions.description: Retrieves the opaque pointer and optionally the object's class ID, regardless of class. Returns NULL if no opaque or not a custom class.
requirements: class_id may be NULL or a pointer to receive the class id.

functions.name: JS_ParseJSON
functions.signature: JSValue JS_ParseJSON(JSContext *ctx, const char *buf, size_t buf_len, const char *filename);
functions.description: Parses JSON from a buffer. buf must be zero-terminated at buf[buf_len]. Returns the parsed value or JS_EXCEPTION.
requirements: buf must have a NUL terminator at buf[buf_len].
filename is a NUL-terminated C string used for error reporting.
Caller must free returned JSValue or handle JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_JSONStringify
functions.signature: JSValue JS_JSONStringify(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst obj, JSValueConst replacer, JSValueConst space0);
functions.description: Serializes a JS value to a JSON string with optional replacer and space. Returns a string or JS_EXCEPTION.
requirements: Caller must free returned JSValue or handle JS_EXCEPTION.

Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_NewArrayBufferCopy
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewArrayBufferCopy(JSContext *ctx, const uint8_t *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Creates a new ArrayBuffer with a copy of the provided data.
requirements: buf must point to at least len bytes.
Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_DetachArrayBuffer
functions.description: Detaches an ArrayBuffer, rendering its underlying storage inaccessible.
requirements: obj must be an ArrayBuffer; not consumed.

functions.name: JS_GetArrayBuffer
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the underlying ArrayBuffer data and optionally its size. Returns NULL if obj is not an ArrayBuffer.
requirements: psize may be NULL or a valid pointer to receive size.
Returned pointer is only valid while the ArrayBuffer remains attached and alive.

functions.name: JS_IsArrayBuffer
functions.description: Returns true if the value is an ArrayBuffer.

functions.name: JS_GetUint8Array
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the backing store for a Uint8Array and its byte length, or NULL if not a Uint8Array.
requirements: psize may be NULL or pointer to receive size.

functions.name: JS_NewTypedArray
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewTypedArray(JSContext *ctx, int argc, JSValueConst *argv, JSTypedArrayEnum array_type);
functions.description: Creates a typed array based on the provided arguments and type. Semantics follow JS constructors for typed arrays.
requirements: argv must point to argc arguments; not consumed.
array_type must be a valid JSTypedArrayEnum value.
Caller must free the returned JSValue.

functions.name: JS_GetTypedArrayBuffer
functions.signature: JSValue JS_GetTypedArrayBuffer(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst obj, size_t *pbyte_offset, size_t *pbyte_length, size_t *pbytes_per_element);
functions.description: Returns the ArrayBuffer backing a typed array along with offset, length, and bytes-per-element. Returns JS_EXCEPTION on failure.
requirements: obj must be a typed array; not consumed.
Output pointers may be NULL or valid addresses to receive info.
Caller must free returned JSValue (the ArrayBuffer) or handle JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_NewUint8Array
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewUint8Array(JSContext *ctx, uint8_t *buf, size_t len, JSFreeArrayBufferDataFunc *free_func, void *opaque, bool is_shared);
functions.description: Creates a Uint8Array view over an external buffer. free_func is invoked on buffer release if provided.
requirements: buf must point to at least len bytes.
free_func may be NULL; otherwise must be callable with (rt, opaque, buf).

functions.name: JS_GetTypedArrayType
functions.description: Returns the typed array type (JSTypedArrayEnum) for a typed array, or -1 if not a typed array.

functions.name: JS_NewUint8ArrayCopy
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewUint8ArrayCopy(JSContext *ctx, const uint8_t *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Creates a new Uint8Array initialized with a copy of the provided bytes.
requirements: buf must point to at least len bytes.

functions.name: JS_SetSharedArrayBufferFunctions
functions.description: Sets allocation and lifetime hooks for SharedArrayBuffer backing memory.
requirements: sf must point to a fully initialized JSSharedArrayBufferFunctions struct; function pointers may be NULL depending on intended behavior.

functions.name: JS_NewPromiseCapability
functions.description: Creates a new Promise and stores the resolve and reject functions into resolving_funcs[0] and resolving_funcs[1]. Returns the Promise object.
requirements: resolving_funcs must point to space for 2 JSValue entries. The function populates them; caller owns and must free them.
Caller must free returned Promise value.

functions.name: JS_PromiseState
functions.description: Returns the state of a Promise, or JS_PROMISE_NOT_A_PROMISE if input is not a Promise.

functions.name: JS_PromiseResult
functions.description: Returns the result (fulfillment value or rejection reason) of a settled Promise. Behavior on pending promises is implementation-defined.
requirements: Caller must free returned JSValue or handle JS_EXCEPTION.

functions.name: JS_IsPromise
functions.description: Returns true if the value is a Promise object.

functions.name: JS_NewSymbol
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewSymbol(JSContext *ctx, const char *description, bool is_global);
functions.description: Creates a new Symbol with an optional description. If is_global is true, creates or retrieves a global symbol with that key.
requirements: description may be NULL or a NUL-terminated C string.

functions.name: JS_SetPromiseHook
functions.description: Registers a hook for promise lifecycle events (init/before/after/resolve).
requirements: promise_hook may be NULL to clear hooks.
opaque is passed back to the hook as provided.

functions.name: JS_SetHostPromiseRejectionTracker
functions.description: Registers a callback for unhandled/handled promise rejections.
requirements: cb may be NULL to clear.
opaque is user data passed to callback.

functions.name: JS_SetInterruptHandler
functions.description: Sets an interrupt handler that can abort JS execution when it returns non-zero.
requirements: cb may be NULL to clear.
opaque is passed to the handler.

functions.name: JS_SetCanBlock
functions.description: Enables or disables the ability for Atomics.wait() to block in this runtime.

functions.name: JS_SetIsHTMLDDA
functions.description: Sets the [IsHTMLDDA] internal slot on an object (special web compatibility behavior).
requirements: obj not consumed; should be an object.

functions.name: JS_SetModuleLoaderFunc
functions.description: Registers module normalization and loading callbacks (without import attributes support). module_normalize may be NULL to use default.
requirements: module_loader must be a valid function pointer; module_normalize may be NULL.
opaque is user data passed to callbacks.

functions.name: JS_SetModuleLoaderFunc2
functions.signature: void JS_SetModuleLoaderFunc2(JSRuntime *rt, JSModuleNormalizeFunc *module_normalize, JSModuleLoaderFunc2 *module_loader, JSModuleCheckSupportedImportAttributes *module_check_attrs, void *opaque);
functions.description: Registers module loader callbacks with import-attributes support and an attribute checker.
requirements: module_loader must be valid; module_normalize and module_check_attrs may be NULL as needed.
opaque is user data passed to callbacks.

functions.name: JS_GetImportMeta
functions.description: Returns the import.meta object for a module.
requirements: m must be a valid module pointer.

functions.name: JS_GetModuleName
functions.description: Returns the module name as an atom. Must be freed with JS_FreeAtom.
requirements: m must be a valid module pointer.
Caller must release the returned atom with JS_FreeAtom(ctx, atom).

functions.name: JS_GetModuleNamespace

import random
import struct
import itertools
from typing import List

# This generator targets QuickJS fuzzers that request arbitrary binary strings
# and filenames. The fuzz stubs frequently use FUZZ_PARAM_STR as:
# - JavaScript source that must be NUL-terminated at input[input_len]
# - JSON strings that must be NUL-terminated at buf[buf_len]
# - Binary buffers for JS_NewStringLen/JS_NewAtomLen (explicit length)
# - Byte contents for ArrayBuffer/TypedArray copy constructors
#
# Strategy
# - Produce a compact bytes buffer (<=4096 bytes) that contains multiple
#   concatenated segments separated by a sentinel so that different consumers
#   can slice meaningful data for len selections inside stubs.
# - Include a variety of ASCII/UTF-8 JS snippets likely to parse/evaluate,
#   valid JSON, and random binary (including NULs) for ArrayBuffer/UTF-16 tests.
# - Include edge-case lengths and characters to exercise comparison paths.
# - Keep buffer self-contained and not perform any I/O.
#
# Layout
# [Header][Segments joined with delimiter b"\x00\xff\x00\xfe"][Trailer]
# The presence of interior NULs is fine (binary string). Stubs typically choose
# a length modulo size; many will also append a NUL at chosen length.

DELIM = b"\x00\xff\x00\xfe"
MAX_SIZE = 4096

JS_SNIPPETS = [
    b"",  # empty
    b"1+1",
    b"(function(){return 42})()",
    b"var x=10, y=32; x+y",
    b"'hello' + ' world'",
    b"let a=[1,2,3]; a.length",
    b"({a:1,b:2}).a",
    b"new Date(0).getUTCFullYear()",
    b"({toString(){return 'obj'}}+0)",
    b"(async function(){return 5})().then(v=>v)",
    b"try{throw new Error('e')}catch(e){e.name}",
    b"/a*b+c?/.test('abccc')",
    b"typeof Symbol('d')",
    b"JSON.stringify({k:1})",
    b"class C{constructor(x){this.x=x}}; new C(7).x",
]

JSON_SNIPPETS = [
    b"{}",
    b"[]",
    b"{\"a\":1}",
    b"[1,2,3]",
    b"{\"nested\":{\"x\":[true,false,null,0,\"s\"]}}",
]

STRINGS_FOR_ATOMS = [
    b"a",
    b"abc",
    b"prop_name",
    b"unicode_\xe2\x98\x83",  # snowman UTF-8
    b"number_123456",
    b"",
]

# Produce some binary blobs with varied distributions, including NULs.

def random_binary(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def patterned_binary(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Repeating short patterns and incremental sequences
    patterns = [b"\x00", b"\xff", b"\x00\x01\x02\x03", b"AB", b"XYZ", b"\x7f\x80\x00\x01"]
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < n:
        p = rng.choice(patterns)
        reps = rng.randint(1, 8)
        out.extend(p * reps)
    return bytes(out[:n])


def utf16_bytes_from_utf8_prefix(data: bytes, max_units: int) -> bytes:
    # Map each byte to a uint16 code unit; used by JS_NewStringUTF16 stub
    units = data[:max_units]
    b = bytearray()
    for ch in units:
        b.extend(struct.pack('<H', ch))  # native-endian; little-endian common
    return bytes(b)


def build_segments(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    segs: List[bytes] = []

    # JavaScript sources (likely valid)
    rng.shuffle(JS_SNIPPETS)
    for s in JS_SNIPPETS[:rng.randint(5, len(JS_SNIPPETS))]:
        segs.append(s)

    # JSON payloads
    rng.shuffle(JSON_SNIPPETS)
    for j in JSON_SNIPPETS[:rng.randint(3, len(JSON_SNIPPETS))]:
        segs.append(j)

    # Atom/name strings
    for a in STRINGS_FOR_ATOMS:
        segs.append(a)

    # Numbers encoded as ASCII for string/number comparisons
    nums = [b"0", b"1", b"-1", b"1234567890", b"3.14159", b"1e+308", b"NaN", b"Infinity", b"-0"]
    segs.extend(nums)

    # Random binary and patterned chunks including NUL bytes
    for _ in range(6):
        n = rng.randint(1, 256)
        segs.append(random_binary(rng, n))
        segs.append(patterned_binary(rng, n))

    # UTF-16 like buffer bytes (as raw bytes; callers that need UTF-16 will read prefix)
    base = random_binary(rng, rng.randint(8, 128))
    segs.append(utf16_bytes_from_utf8_prefix(base, rng.randint(4, min(64, len(base)))))

    # Some edge-case segments
    segs.append(b"\x00" * rng.randint(0, 64))  # all NULs
    segs.append(b"\xff" * rng.randint(1, 64))  # all 0xFF

    return segs


def assemble(segs: List[bytes], rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Interleave with delimiter; ensure final size <= MAX_SIZE
    out = bytearray()
    # Optional header with a small magic and version-like bytes
    header = b"QJ" + struct.pack('<H', 1) + DELIM
    out.extend(header)

    for s in segs:
        if len(out) + len(s) + len(DELIM) > MAX_SIZE:
            break
        out.extend(s)
        out.extend(DELIM)

    # Trailer with a few sentinel bytes
    trailer = b"END" + struct.pack('<I', len(out))
    max_trailer = MAX_SIZE - len(out)
    trailer = trailer[:max_trailer]
    out.extend(trailer)
    return bytes(out[:MAX_SIZE])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build segments with mixed valid JS/JSON and binary content
    segs = build_segments(rng)

    # Randomly shuffle to vary early prefixes
    rng.shuffle(segs)

    buf = assemble(segs, rng)

    # As a final tweak, ensure buffer isn't empty and sometimes prepend a short
    # JavaScript prelude to help JS_Eval/JS_DetectModule success paths.
    if not buf:
        buf = b"1+1\n"
    else:
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            prelude = rng.choice(JS_SNIPPETS)
            pre = prelude + b"\n" if prelude else b""
            candidate = pre + buf
            buf = candidate[:MAX_SIZE]

    return buf

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: C string (UTF-8/ASCII)
# We need to generate a single bytes buffer that the fuzzing framework will
# split to feed FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME(). Those expect
# NUL-terminated C strings without embedded NULs.
#
# Goals for interesting inputs:
# - Vary lengths: empty string, short, medium, near 4KB cap.
# - Include ASCII control edge cases and punctuation but avoid NUL inside.
# - Include valid multi-byte UTF-8 sequences (e.g., emojis, CJK, combining marks).
# - Property-like identifiers, numbers, mixed cases, long repeats.
# - Filenames/paths: absolute/relative, with directories, extensions, unusual but valid characters.
# - JavaScript-ident-like names and typical module filenames.
#
# Encoding format for the buffer:
# - Concatenate several NUL-terminated strings one after another so the fuzzer
#   can pull multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR()/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() values from the
#   same buffer.
# - No embedded NULs within each string content; each string ends with a single NUL byte.
# - Limit total buffer size to <= 4096 bytes.

ASCII_SAFE = (
    string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.:,+/\\@#%[](){}!$^&=~'`"  # no NUL
)

# Some valid multi-byte UTF-8 snippets to spice strings up
UNICODE_SNIPPETS = [
    "π", "µ", "✓", "©", "™", "€", "—", "–", "…",
    "你好", "こんにちは", "Привет", "مرحبا", "हैलो",
    "😀", "🧪", "🚀", "📝", "🔒", "📦",
    "á",  # a + combining acute
]

# Common JS-like identifiers and property names
IDENTS = [
    "",  # empty string variant
    "a", "A", "_", "$",
    "length", "constructor", "prototype", "__proto__", "toString",
    "value", "get", "set", "then", "catch", "finally",
    "map", "set", "has", "delete", "size",
]

# Common file/module names and extensions
FILENAMES = [
    "",  # empty -> may exercise failure paths gracefully
    "index.js", "main.js", "mod.mjs", "lib.cjs",
    "data.json", "config.json", "a.txt",
    "script.min.js", "emoji-😀.js", "π_math.js",
    "./relative.js", "../up/module.js", "/abs/path/module.js",
    "C:\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\etc\\hosts",  # Windows-y path
    "./dir.with.dots/file.name.jsx",
]

EXTS = [".js", ".mjs", ".cjs", ".json", ".txt"]


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    return "".join(rng.choice(ASCII_SAFE) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_unicode(rng: random.Random, n_snippets: int) -> str:
    parts: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(n_snippets):
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            parts.append(_rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(1, 8)))
        parts.append(rng.choice(UNICODE_SNIPPETS))
    return "".join(parts)


def _make_identifier(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Start with letter/_/$ then mix digits and letters
    start = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + "_$")
    length = rng.randint(0, 20)
    rest_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_$"
    rest = "".join(rng.choice(rest_chars) for _ in range(length))
    # Occasionally sprinkle unicode
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        rest += rng.choice(UNICODE_SNIPPETS)
    return start + rest


def _make_prop_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    choices = IDENTS + [
        _make_identifier(rng),
        _make_identifier(rng).lower(),
        _make_identifier(rng).upper(),
        str(rng.randint(-100000, 100000)),
    ]
    s = rng.choice(choices)
    # sometimes dot-separated path-like properties
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        parts = [s] + [_make_identifier(rng) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3))]
        s = ".".join(parts)
    return s


def _make_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # 50% from curated list
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return rng.choice(FILENAMES)
    # Otherwise synthesize path
    parts: List[str] = []
    # absolute or relative
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append("/")
    depth = rng.randint(0, 4)
    for _ in range(depth):
        seg_len = rng.randint(1, 12)
        seg = _rand_ascii(rng, seg_len).strip()
        seg = seg.strip("/") or "dir"
        parts.append(seg)
    name = _make_identifier(rng)
    # maybe add unicode in filename
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        name += rng.choice(["-", "_"]) + rng.choice(UNICODE_SNIPPETS)
    ext = rng.choice(EXTS)
    parts.append(name + ext)
    path = "/".join(p for p in parts if p)
    # Occasionally Windows-style
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        path = path.replace("/", "\\")
    return path


def _bounded(s: str, max_len: int) -> str:
    # ensure no embedded NUL and clip length
    s = s.replace("\x00", " ")
    if len(s.encode("utf-8")) > max_len:
        # approximate cut by characters, then enforce by bytes below
        s = s[: max_len]
        # ensure by bytes strictly
        b = s.encode("utf-8")[:max_len]
        s = b.decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    return s


def _terminate(s: str) -> bytes:
    return s.encode("utf-8") + b"\x00"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Plan a mix of strings used by the stubs:
    # - Several general-purpose strings for JS_NewAtom, JS_*PropertyStr, js_strdup, etc.
    # - Several filenames for JS_LoadModule/js_load_file and other filename-accepting APIs.
    # Keep total under 4096 bytes.

    pieces: List[bytes] = []
    budget = 4096

    # Always include some canonical interesting strings
    base_strings: List[str] = [
        "",  # empty
        "a", "0", "_", "$",
        "constructor", "__proto__", "toString", "then", "catch",
        "1234567890", "name", "length",
        "emoji-😀", "π_math", "hello-世界",
        _rand_ascii(rng, 32),
        _rand_unicode(rng, 4),
        _make_prop_like(rng),
        _make_prop_like(rng),
    ]

    # Add a few random-length ASCII and unicode strings
    for _ in range(rng.randint(4, 8)):
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            s = _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(1, 80))
        else:
            s = _rand_unicode(rng, rng.randint(1, 6))
        base_strings.append(s)

    # Some long strings near limit for stress (but still valid)
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        long_len = rng.randint(256, 1024)
        base_strings.append(_rand_ascii(rng, long_len))
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        base_strings.append(_rand_unicode(rng, rng.randint(20, 60)))

    # Filenames
    filename_strings: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(4, 8)):
        filename_strings.append(_make_filename(rng))

    # Interleave to provide variety for successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FILENAME pulls
    all_strings: List[str] = []
    # Start with a filename then a generic, alternating
    while base_strings or filename_strings:
        if filename_strings:
            all_strings.append(filename_strings.pop(0))
        if base_strings:
            all_strings.append(base_strings.pop(0))

    # Bound and pack with NUL terminators respecting total budget
    for s in all_strings:
        # leave some room for the NUL and avoid exceeding budget
        max_for_this = max(0, budget - 1)
        if max_for_this <= 0:
            break
        s_bounded = _bounded(s, max_for_this)
        entry = _terminate(s_bounded)
        if len(entry) > budget:
            # Try to shrink further if needed
            shrink = _bounded(s_bounded, max(0, budget - 1))
            entry = _terminate(shrink)
        if len(entry) <= budget:
            pieces.append(entry)
            budget -= len(entry)
        else:
            break

    # Ensure we have at least one NUL-terminated empty string if nothing added
    if not pieces:
        pieces.append(b"\x00")

    return b"".join(pieces)
